reviews.author: Evan Wrede
reviews.text: I moved to South Jersey and began using Goodies at a friends recommendation. They now service my family’s three cars. I cannot stress enough what good people these are and incredibly fair in their advice and pricing. When my truck recently had catastrophic engine failure, I knew exactly where I was going. James took the time to explain what needed to be done and had ALOT of experience with the repair as it’s a common problem with my make, model and year. Do yourself a favor and give this business your business…you won’t be sorry!

reviews.author: Kyle Rebman
reviews.text: Called in for a quote for a transmission fluid and filter change for a Chevy Silverado. I first asked "does your business service transmissions?" And the response was "yes". So I then asked for a quote and when I could schedule the service. I was then told "I needed to setup a diagnosis appointment first" and that "they don't give quotes over the phone". Sorry, but since when were diagnosis' required for routine maintenance? I didnt say my transmission is acting weird and I don't know why. I asked for a routine service and quote for that service which should be 1-2 fixed values depending on if an exhaust pipe needs to be moved to drop the pan. I'd understand if this wasn't black and white to quote out, but it is. I can't comprehend this type of nonsense response other than an attempt at a cash grab. I called a different place and got my transmission preventatively serviced. No "diagnosis" and was told the price over the phone as expected. Edit: So can we not read or comprehend English? What are we dancing around my point for and bringing up hypotheticals like "customer brought parts"? Or are we assuming im "price shopping"? Because I wasn't. As an adult, I don't just ask for a service without asking what the associated cost is. So that's what that was. But let me crystal clear: I asked for a transmission fluid and filter change. I was told a diagnosis was needed first. Full stop. Why? Why is a diagnosis needed for a ROUTINE service? This is NOT standard practice. I've always gotten my transmissions serviced by mechanics for my entire life amongst 6 different vehicles. I've never had this response to this service request, ever. But by your logic, every other mechanic I've been to in my past sucks and they're not busy, right? How about this: next time just say you don't do basic transmission fluid changes. Because you don't need a "diagnosis" for that. Not every person asking for a service from a mechanic is completely clueless on how vehicles work to understand when something makes zero sense. I will continue giving my patronage to other mechanics that are just as fabulous as you are. Finally, when you say "we and other shops don't give quotes over phone for" whatever reason, you are in the minority. The review is for other people to know that, and you've made it crystal clear. Have a blessed day.

reviews.text: Goodies auto has been nothing but extremely honest and helpful. I have a jeep wrangler and it has had alot of problems and broken parts in it but every time i need something fixed its done within the next 2 or 3 days of me dropping it of i have nothing but high respect for a mechanic that will tell you exactly whats wrong with your vehicle and doesnt charge you an arm and a leg to fix everything especially when they diagnose the vehicle for free to tell you whats wrong with it. This is crew is made up of TRUE mechanics, which are slim to none nowadays. I highly recommend them for any of your vehicle needs. reviews.author: Ryan Stransky
reviews.text: I will start this review off by saying that while I have not had any work done by this business, I had an experience recently where the owner, whose name I sadly forget, went out of his way to help out myself and my fiance. On January 20th, we went to the philly auto show and as per usual we paid to park in the lot we park in every year. Long story short, the parking lot staff made it to where I could not get my truck out of my parking spot because they basically blocked me in. If I could find them on Google I'd blast them a 1 star review. But when the man saw that was pretty much stuck, he offered help right off the bat and then he grabbed a tow strap and a shackle from the back of his gold colored duramax, and he hooked up to my truck and pulled my tail end to help me get out of the parking spot without touching any other vehicles. It's hard to give a good explanation of the situation, but it's strictly because of his kindness and willingness to help that we were able to leave that lot and head home He told me the silver dually in the custom section was his and that he had a shoo in jersey. From my photos of his truck, I found his business page and now here I am. The man not only helped big time, but he refused a cash payment from me. So I am here to say thank you again and to let all the people know that this is genuinely a good stand up dude running this business. His good deed that day is surely a testament to him as a person and as a business man. I will be reaching out to this shop once I order my lift kit for my f150. 5 stars all the way!

reviews.author: Michael Valvardi
reviews.text: Goodies seems to be as good as you can get! I had a recent great experience using Goodies Automotive Service for an emergency repair. My 2000 F350 front end started wobbling on the highway and I limped if off and wound up taking it to Goodies since they were nearby (I read the reviews for shops local to where I was and those that could accommodate a large truck and also were known for suspension repairs). The mechanics I normally use for my wife’s car can’t accommodate a large and heavy truck (crew cab, long bed, 7.3 engine). I explained I was not in a hurry when I made the appointment, however Goodies took in my truck the very next day. That same day they informed me of what needed to be repaired, some necessary and others optional. The truck was fixed the day after that (front wheel bearings, one inner tie rod, drag link, track bar, adjuster sleeve, and front shocks). There was absolutely no pressure to do the optional work. I had no expectation of this quick turnaround: made the appointment Wednesday afternoon, dropped off the truck Thursday and the truck was evaluated that day. The repairs were then completed by noon on Friday. Goodies made sure I was satisfied with the work and ensured that the steering wheel was centered after making all the final adjustments to the new components. Very good communication with everyone I dealt with at Goodies.

reviews.author: Greg Gablin

reviews.author: george miller
reviews.text: Dropped off a car for a customer and they praised how awesome goodies was. Will definitely be checking them out

reviews.author: christian murphy
reviews.text: Would definitely recommend this place for all of your automotive needs they do it all! appreciate all the help thank you James !!!

reviews.author: Michael Viriato
reviews.text: Had a great experience with this shop after being recommended by a friend . James is very knowledgeable, honest, and straight-up about everything. New headers and intake manifold came out great, and the whole process was smooth and professional. Highly recommend this shop and will definitely be coming back for future work.

reviews.author: Jake Matlock
reviews.text: Genuinely one of the best shops you’ll find anywhere in New Jersey. Goodies has done the rear end, downpipes, and suspension on my F-150, and after 100,000+ miles, every component is still holding strong. James stands behind his work, and the quality is consistently there. The attention to detail, workmanship, and honesty are hard to find these days. I’ve sent numerous friends their way, and every one of them has come back happy. If you care about your vehicle and want the job done right, I can’t recommend Goodies enough.
